title: One of Each
statement: A sorted array of ticket numbers contains repeats. Remove the repeats in place, so that each number appears once at the front of the array in sorted order, without creating a second array. Return the unique numbers (the front part of the array).
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

answerKey.pattern: Overwrite in place with a write index; because the array is sorted, a repeat always equals the last value written
keyPoints: Keep a write index w for the next unique value; the first value is always kept
For each value, write it only if it differs from the last value written (nums[w - 1])
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space (not counting the returned copy)
acceptableSlowerApproaches: A hash set of seen values: O(n) time but O(n) extra space and ignores that the array is sorted
Deleting each repeat and shifting: O(n²)

hints: Because the array is sorted, where can a repeat of a value be?
Repeats sit right next to each other. Compare each value with the last value you kept, not with every earlier value.
Use a write index: when a value differs from nums[w - 1], copy it to nums[w] and move w forward.
